investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-07-02T10:41–10:48Z because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected by the Kubernetes scheduler: 2 of 6 nodes reported Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the pod never reached a running state, so the eval contract was violated at the earliest possible point — VM scheduling — before any agent lifecycle logic could execute.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted the allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that are eligible for peer-pod scheduling. The remaining 4 nodes are ineligible due to node affinity or label selector mismatch. With zero schedulable capacity and no preemption victims available, every remote-agent pod is stuck Unschedulable, preventing VM provisioning and causing all three remote-agent checks to fail with identical scheduler messages. This is an infrastructure-layer capacity constraint, not an application code defect. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence; this is an eval-detected failure.

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:250-258: contract requires vmIdPresent=true and remoteState oneOf [running, idle, ready] — neither assertion could be evaluated because the pod never started.
possibleCauses: [Most likely] kata.peerpods.io/vm resource quota is fully consumed on the 2 eligible nodes — existing remote agent VMs or other peer-pod workloads have claimed all available slots, leaving no capacity for new probe pods.

[Likely] The 4 non-peer-pod nodes have a node affinity or label selector that excludes them from remote-agent pods (e.g., a required node label or taint for kata/peer-pod runtime is absent), reducing effective scheduling capacity to only 2 nodes.
[Possible] A prior eval run or leaked agent from a previous withCleanup cycle left a VM allocated on one or both eligible nodes, consuming the remaining capacity without being released.
[Possible] The 2 kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes are in a degraded or cordoned state that prevents preemption from reclaiming slots, as indicated by 'No preemption victims found for incoming pod'.

[Lower likelihood] A recent cluster configuration change reduced the advertised kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity per node (e.g., a node pool resize or resource limit adjustment), but no infrastructure change evidence is present in the supplied packet.

investigation.title: Remote Agents: All Three Checks Failing — Kubernetes Cluster Exhausted of kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api on 2026-07-02 with identical Kubernetes scheduling errors: the 6-node cluster has zero schedulable nodes for new kata peer-pod VMs, with 2 nodes reporting insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and 4 nodes failing pod affinity/selector matching. Because no agent pod could be scheduled, the eval runner's createAgent call never returned a live agent, so no evidence (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) was ever written and the expected-output contract was fully violated.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents swarm (production-api environment) has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource quota across the 2 nodes that carry that resource class. The remaining 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity/selector requirements. As a result, every attempt to schedule a remote-agent pod during the eval window was rejected as Unschedulable, no VM was provisioned, and the eval runner could not progress past createAgent to collect any required evidence. This is an infrastructure-layer scheduling failure localized to the remote-agents VM pool, not a code regression in the eval runner itself. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence; impact is scoped to this observability eval.

possibleCauses: PRIMARY — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 eligible nodes: all available VM slots on the peer-pod-capable nodes are occupied by existing workloads, leaving no capacity for new eval pods. Preemption was also ruled out ('No preemption victims found'), indicating no lower-priority pods are evictable.

SECONDARY — Node affinity/selector mismatch on 4 of 6 nodes: the remote-agent pod spec requires a node label or taint that only 2 nodes carry (the kata peer-pod nodes), and those 2 are already at capacity. A misconfiguration or drift in node labels could reduce the eligible pool further.

TERTIARY — Cluster-level quota or LimitRange on kata.peerpods.io/vm: a namespace or cluster resource quota may cap the number of concurrent peer-pod VMs below what the eval run requires, causing exhaustion even if physical node capacity exists.

LOWER — Transient spike in concurrent remote-agent workloads at the time of the eval run (10:43–10:48 UTC) consuming all VM slots before the eval pods could be scheduled; this would be a timing/contention issue rather than a persistent capacity deficit.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-07-02T10:41–10:48Z because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected by the Kubernetes scheduler: 2 of 6 nodes reported Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the pod never reached a running state, so the eval contract was violated at the earliest possible point — VM scheduling — before any agent lifecycle logic could execute.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted the allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that are eligible for peer-pod scheduling. The remaining 4 nodes are ineligible due to node affinity or label selector mismatch. With zero schedulable capacity and no preemption victims available, every remote-agent pod is stuck Unschedulable, preventing VM provisioning and causing all three remote-agent checks to fail with identical scheduler messages. This is an infrastructure-layer capacity constraint, not an application code defect. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence; this is an eval-detected failure.

sibling.remote-agent-runtime: identical Unschedulable root cause, latencyMs=146835, endedAt=2026-07-02T10:48:36.088Z — confirms the condition persisted for the full ~7-minute observation window.

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:250-258: contract requires vmIdPresent=true and remoteState oneOf [running, idle, ready] — neither assertion could be evaluated because the pod never started.
possibleCauses: [Most likely] kata.peerpods.io/vm resource quota is fully consumed on the 2 eligible nodes — existing remote agent VMs or other peer-pod workloads have claimed all available slots, leaving no capacity for new probe pods.

[Likely] The 4 non-peer-pod nodes have a node affinity or label selector that excludes them from remote-agent pods (e.g., a required node label or taint for kata/peer-pod runtime is absent), reducing effective scheduling capacity to only 2 nodes.
[Possible] A prior eval run or leaked agent from a previous withCleanup cycle left a VM allocated on one or both eligible nodes, consuming the remaining capacity without being released.
[Possible] The 2 kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes are in a degraded or cordoned state that prevents preemption from reclaiming slots, as indicated by 'No preemption victims found for incoming pod'.

[Lower likelihood] A recent cluster configuration change reduced the advertised kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity per node (e.g., a node pool resize or resource limit adjustment), but no infrastructure change evidence is present in the supplied packet.
